assertions.name: Direct substitution of [2]_q over-predicts T_boil for every material
assertions.source: T_boil_pred = S_q / ([2]_q R) misses high everywhere: H2O 6.45x, HF 5.04x, NH3 4.26x (range 4.26-6.45x, NOT the 6-10x the previous assertion name claimed — see bean qou-3hre)

description: Attempts to derive absolute boiling and freezing temperatures strictly from the q-ideal gas law (q-PV = nRT) without fitted scaling factors. Computes the cohesion energy from the h²-suppressed H-bond network, then sets T_boil = S_q / (n_q R). With the naive choice n_q = [2]_q (the dimension of the Hopf base exploring S²), this over-predicts the temperatures by a factor of 6.4x to 10x. This demonstrates that the true entropy of vaporisation ΔS_vap requires a more sophisticated topological partition function (likely involving the full Reeb flow phase space) rather than just the bare dimension [2]_q. Result is recorded honestly as open.

data.finding: The bare mapping P_q V_q = [2]_q R T over-predicts T_boil and T_melt by 6-10x. A derived topological factor for ΔS_vap is required. No fit applied. Status remains OPEN.
